help.running-an-election.title: Running an election
help.running-an-election.summary: Setting the two date windows, choosing which part of the family votes, putting offices on the ballot, and publishing it.
help.running-an-election.what-it-is.head: What this screen is
help.running-an-election.what-it-is.b0: Every election the family has, at every level, drafts included. Each row shows where the election is today, which part of the family it is for, its two date windows, and how many positions, nominations and votes it has.
help.running-an-election.what-it-is.b1: **New Election** opens the form in a panel over the list, and so does the edit control on a draft. The list stays behind it, which is the point — you can see what the family already holds while you write the next one.
help.running-an-election.what-it-is.b2: An election is either a **draft** — yours, invisible to the family — or **published**, which puts it on the family' calendar. There is nothing else to set: once it is published the dates run it.
help.running-an-election.the-windows.b0: **Nominations** and **Voting**, each with an opening date and a closing date. They are what makes the election happen; nobody has to come back and press anything.
Nominations run from the day they open to the end of the day they close. Both days count.
Voting runs the same way, and may not open BEFORE nominations close — a ballot is never voted on while the list of candidates can still change.

It may open on the same day they close, and then that day belongs to voting: nominations shut as the ballot opens. That is the shortest election the product can describe — one day of nominations, one day of voting. Give nominations the whole of their closing day by setting it a day earlier.
Each window has to be at least a day long. A closing date on or before its opening date is refused as you type it.

The date pickers grey out the days that would break the chain — once nominations open on the 1st, the closing picker will not offer the 1st or anything before it, and the voting pickers move with it. The voting opening picker DOES offer the day nominations close, because that one is allowed.
help.running-an-election.the-windows.b2: The day after voting closes, the election is over and its results appear for everybody who could vote in it. Nothing publishes them and nothing closes the poll.
help.running-an-election.the-windows.b3: All four dates are needed to publish. A draft may have none of them, or some — that is what a draft is for.
help.running-an-election.the-level.b0: **Who votes** picks the level: the whole family, one region, or one chapter. It decides three things at once, and they are not separable.
help.running-an-election.the-level.b1.i0: Who can SEE the election. A chapter election is not listed for the rest of the family and its link does not open for them.
help.running-an-election.the-level.b1.i1: Who can be NOMINATED. The nominee list on the ballot holds only the people the election is for.
help.running-an-election.the-level.b1.i2: Which OFFICES it can fill — only those recorded at the same level under [Board positions](/help/board-positions).
help.running-an-election.the-level.b2: Changing the level after you have chosen positions clears any that no longer belong to it, and says which. That is not the form losing your work; it is the rule that an election cannot fill an office from another level.
help.running-an-election.the-level.b3: A family with no regions and no chapters gets National and nothing else, because there is nothing to point at. Regions and chapters are set up under [Regions & chapters](/help/regions-and-chapters).
help.running-an-election.the-level.b4: Members who are not in a chapter are under National. They take part in national elections and in no scoped one, so an election narrowed to a chapter is narrower than it may look — check who is actually filed there before publishing one.
help.running-an-election.positions.b0: **Positions** is the list of offices this election fills. Each one is chosen from the family' board roster at the matching level, and **Winners** is how many people the office seats — usually one.
help.running-an-election.positions.b1: An office you expected and cannot find is either recorded at a different level or not recorded at all. Add or re-scope it under [Board positions](/help/board-positions) first.
help.running-an-election.positions.b2: An election needs at least one position before it can be published.
help.running-an-election.publishing.head: Publishing it
help.running-an-election.publishing.b0.i: Fill the form in and press **Create draft**. Nothing is visible to the family yet.
Read the row back — the level, both windows, and the number of positions.
Leave **Announce** ticked if you want the family told, then press **Publish** and confirm.
help.running-an-election.publishing.b1: The announcement is addressed the way the election is: a chapter election is announced to that chapter. A regional one goes to the whole family and names the region, because an announcement can be addressed to a chapter and not to a region.
help.running-an-election.publishing.b2: **The notice is a way in.** Its title is a link straight to the election, on the board and in the **Recent Updates** card on the [Dashboard](/dashboard) alike, so nobody has to go looking for the ballot they have just been told about. A member whose family has switched Elections off, or is not on a plan that includes them, sees the notice without the link rather than a link that refuses them.
help.running-an-election.publishing.b3: After that there is nothing to do. Nominations open on their date, close on theirs, voting opens and closes on its own, and the results appear.
help.running-an-election.watching-it.b0: The arrow at the end of any row opens that election's own screen — the organizer's view of it, not the ballot. Four figures across the top:
Approved members of this election's part of the family who have an account. Somebody recorded on the family tree with no account of their own can be nominated and cannot vote, so they are not counted here.
How many of them have, and the turnout that works out to.
The difference. It is a number and never a list — nobody is named, here or anywhere.
Accepted nominations against total nominations. A nomination nobody has answered is not on the ballot, and only accepted candidates can be voted for.
help.running-an-election.watching-it.b2: Below them, every office with the people standing for it, their vote counts and their share. The leaders carry a trophy, as many as the office seats.
help.running-an-election.watching-it.b3: **While voting is open these are a snapshot, and the screen says so.** Nothing here declares a winner until the window closes; it is there so you can see whether an election is going to work — whether anybody accepted, whether anybody is voting — while there is still time to do something about it.
help.running-an-election.watching-it.b4: This screen never shows which way a named person voted, and nothing anywhere does. See [Elections](/help/elections#voting) for the member's side of that.
help.running-an-election.changing-it.b0: **A draft can be edited freely** — its title, its dates, its level, its positions.
help.running-an-election.changing-it.b1: **A published election cannot be edited.** Its dates are what the family was told, and moving them would change what a ballot was rather than correct a typo.
help.running-an-election.changing-it.b2: **Return to draft** takes a published election back, and is offered only while nobody has been nominated and nothing has been voted on. Once somebody has acted, the election is a record of something the family did: let it run, or delete it.
help.running-an-election.changing-it.b3: **Delete** removes the election with every nomination and vote on it, and cannot be undone. The confirmation says how many of each there are.
help.running-an-election.changing-it.b4: Deleting a region or a chapter an election is scoped to is refused while the election exists — re-scope the election to the whole family first, or delete it. Nothing about the family' shape can quietly change who was entitled to vote.
